title: The Most Important Packers: No. 1 — QB Jordan Love
description: Green Bay's Jordan Love has become one of the NFL's top quarterbacks, but is just 1-3 in the postseason.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers were arguably the most disappointing team in football last year. And perhaps no one did less with more than Packers’ coach Matt LaFleur.

Green Bay headed into the 2025 season with one of the NFL’s top rosters, then traded for star defensive end Micah Parsons 10 days before the year began. Suddenly, Packer Nation was dreaming of their first Super Bowl appearance since 2010.

Instead, Green Bay went a remarkably unsatisfying 9-8-1 overall and was the NFC’s No. 7 seed for a third consecutive year. The Packers then blew a 21-3 halftime lead in the Wild Card round against Chicago, gave up 25 fourth quarter points and eventually suffered a shocking 31-27 loss to the arch-rival Bears.

“No way you should lose games in this league when you’re up that much,” running back Josh Jacobs said.

Green Bay, which began the year 9-3-1, finished the season with five straight losses. The Packers now enter 2026 with the league’s fourth-longest losing streak.

Collapsing late in games was the story of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign.

Green Bay had double digit leads in the final minutes twice against Chicago and also vs. Cleveland and somehow went 0-3 in those games. The Packers’ odds of losing all three contests were 1-in-250,000, yet they somehow did it.

“That (expletive), it’s starting to get damn-near embarrassing,” safety Javon Bullard said.

Rebounding won’t be easy as the Packers were hit hard in free agency and didn't have a first round draft pick.

Green Bay’s first training camp practice is July 29. Between now and then I will count down the ‘30 Most Important Packers’ heading into the 2026 campaign.

For the fourth straight year, quarterback Jordan Love is No. 1.

Love had arguably his finest season yet in 2025.

Love had a career-best passer rating of 101.2 that ranked No. 6 in the NFL. Love completed 291 of 439 passes (66.3%) for 3,381 yards and 23 touchdowns vs. just six interceptions.

Love’s interception percentage was just 1.4% and his touchdown-to-interception ratio was 3.83-1.

Love finished eighth in the league in yards per attempt (7.70) and tied for eighth in explosive passes (16-plus yards) with 81.

When teams blitzed Love, it usually backfired as he posted a 109.5 passer rating against the blitz that ranked fifth in the league.

And while the Packers’ playoff loss to Chicago is one of the more forgettable nights in team history, Love did all he could to lead Green Bay to victory. Love threw four touchdowns, no interceptions and posted a 103.8 passer rating that night in Chicago.

Love, a controversial first round draft pick in 2020, sat for three years behind Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers. Then, when Love got his chance to take over in 2023, he made the most of it.

From 2023-25, Love ranks sixth in the league with 80 touchdowns. He’s also No. 8 in passing yards (10,929) and yards per attempt (7.57).

Love made all 19 starts in 2023, threw 37 touchdown passes and just 13 interceptions. During a two-month window between Week 11 and Green Bay’s NFC divisional playoff game at San Francisco, Love threw a remarkable 23 touchdowns and just one interception.

That’s something Green Bay legends Bart Starr, Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers never did.

Love completed 409 of 634 passes (64.5%) for 4,625 yards and finished with a 98.5 passer rating in 2023. Love ranked second in the league in TD passes and seventh in total passing yards (4,159) that season.

Love signed a four-year, $220 million contract during training camp in 2024, then had an up and down second season as Green Bay’s starter.

Love suffered a sprained medial collateral ligament in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to Philadelphia and missed the next two games. He later missed half of a Week 8 game at Jacksonville with a groin injury and three quarters of a Week 18 loss to Chicago with a right elbow injury.

Despite those injuries, Love threw 25 TDs, 11 interceptions and had a 96.7 passer rating. Love ranked 19th in the league passing yards (3,389) and completed 63.1% of his passes.

Love had a passer rating of at least 107.7 in five straight games between Weeks 11-15, but was at 92.0, or less, the last four contests.

Love then threw three interceptions in Green Bay’s loss to Philadelphia in the NFC Wild Card game and had a season-low passer rating of 41.5.

When the season ended, many suggested Love had regressed in his second season as a starter.

“I mean, what is a step back is what I’d ask?” Love said when asked if he regressed in 2024. “Everybody has different opinions, things like that. You got to block that stuff out.”

Love, who will turn 28 in November, has done his part in carrying on the tremendous quarterback tradition in Green Bay.

He can make every throw. He’s as cool as January night in Green Bay. He’s become more of a vocal leader and he’s highly regarded by his teammates.

Now, the No. 1 question around Love is can he take the Packers on a deep playoff run?

Love won his first playoff game in 2023, but has lost his last three.

Fair or not, players are judged by what they do in the postseason.

There are 35 quarterbacks that have won a Super Bowl. Fifteen are in the Hall of Fame and eight others are locks or likely entrees when they become eligible (Tom Brady, Patrick Mahomes, Drew Brees, Ben Roethlisberger, Aaron Rodgers, Matthew Stafford, Eli Manning and Russell Wilson).

Love has all the tools to become one of the NFL’s elite quarterbacks, but needs to lead Green Bay deep into the playoffs for that narrative to develop.

“Jordan's been awesome, man. Like every year, he just continues to grow as a leader, you know. His consistency is remarkable. Who he is on a daily basis, showing up, how he works, how he leads others, he's pulling guys with them. So I'm really excited about what, you know, is in store for him.” — Packers coach Matt LaFleur on Love

“When I stepped away, it was just two seasons with him, right, so a pretty big difference in maturity, of the command of the offense and also, so it was a quite a few years difference there. But it was just a lot of fun when I step back in it and got to see him really running the show and him in complete control and the comfortability. I think one of his best traits is just that his cool, calm, collected mentality, and then just seeing that match with all the high-level functionality of the mental part of the game. It was really cool to see that when I got back – just a natural growth for his game.” — Packers quarterbacks coach Luke Getsy on Love

“For me, my biggest thing that I’ve noticed since I got back is just my feet in the pocket, trying to be as smooth and consistent as possible. When I go through my reads, get into my hitches and not getting antsy, not getting to that point where you’re trying to move through the pocket too fast. Just staying calm, staying relaxed, move through my reads.” — Love on what he focused on this offseason

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Falcons land WR help in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
description: Falcons take 6-foot-3 Texas WR in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
fullText:
There are some major question marks surrounding the Atlanta Falcons' roster as the team prepares to kick off training camp this week in Flowery Branch. From the starting quarterback competition to the battle for the No. 2 wide receiver job, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski has much to figure out over the next month.

The team signed former first-round pick Jahan Dotson to replace speedster Darnell Mooney, but it's fair to question whether or not he's capable of filling that role. Dotson's career stats suggest otherwise, however, it's tough to produce when you're stuck behind two elite receivers, as he was in Philadelphia.

Former Georgia wide receiver Zachariah Branch appears to have a bright future, assuming his effectiveness isn't hindered by his lack of size. Depending on how this season goes, the Falcons may or may not be looking for a new No. 2 wide receiver in 2027.

Atlanta lands a perfect complement to Drake London in a new CBS Sports mock draft from Mike Renner. The Falcons were projected to take Texas wide receiver Cam Coleman with the sixth overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

"Cam Coleman is a wildly explosive 6-foot-3, 200-pound wideout who spent the past two seasons stuck with poor quarterback play at Auburn," wrote Renner. "That changes this year as he heads to Texas to pair with Arch Manning. He should be a household name by season's end."

Coleman racked up 93 receptions for 1,306 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns (14.0 yards per catch) over the last two seasons at Auburn. The Falcons have dealt with similar quarterback issues over the past few years, so Coleman would feel right at home in Atlanta.

The Falcons did re-sign London to a four-year, $141 million contract extension during the offseason, however, there is still a clear lack of depth behind him. Branch could be a long-term option in the slot with No. 2 upside, but it wouldn't hurt to add to the receiver room in 2027.

For now, Atlanta is set to kick off training camp with its current wide receiver group. Although, we wouldn't be surprised to see the team add someone like Stefon Diggs or Keenan Allen before camp ends.

title: Chiefs’ training camp video of Patrick Mahomes and QB room goes viral
description: The Kansas City Chiefs posted a video of Patrick Mahomes and the QB room throwing passes during training camp. It featured the two-time NFL MVP, along with Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun. They all passed quickly, showcasing that…
fullText:
The Kansas City Chiefs posted a video of Patrick Mahomes and the QB room throwing passes during training camp. It featured the two-time NFL MVP, along with Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun.

They all passed quickly, showcasing that they are in good shape ahead of the 2026 season. Mahomes continues to recover from the torn ACL he sustained in December but looks sharp and not hampered by his injury. The quarterback battle in training camp is expected to be fierce and competitive.

MORE: 7 best fantasy football quarterbacks entering 2026 NFL season

The clip on X has since gone viral, with more than two million views.

Mahomes will reportedly be ready to return as early as Week 1. However, Kansas City is not taking any chances and brought in Justin Fields from the New York Jets to serve as insurance at the position. He has 53 career NFL starts under his belt and will likely be the team’s QB2 once the three-time Super Bowl champion is back to full strength.

Fields joined the Chiefs on March 18 after the franchise sent a 2027 sixth-round pick to New York. They then drafted Nussmeier at No. 249 overall in the seventh round out of LSU. The former Tigers star spent five years with the program and went 5-4 last season.

The Pittsburgh Steelers waived Oladokun in 2022, but he signed a practice squad deal with Kansas City. The team promoted him to the active roster on Dec. 20 following Mahomes’ injury the week prior, and he started his first NFL game on Christmas Day against the Denver Broncos.

The Chiefs will likely ease Mahomes back before he takes over his QB1 job full-time. Fields will serve as his backup, while Nussmeier and Oladokun will battle for the third-string role.

title: ‘This Is Pathetic,’ ‘Always a Victim’ — NFL World Rips Ryan Clark for Crying After Getting Fired by ESPN
description: Super Bowl champion Ryan Clark was among the ESPN staffers laid off last week. This ended his decade-plus run with the network.
fullText:
Super Bowl champion Ryan Clark was among the ESPN staffers laid off last week. This ended his decade-plus run with the network. He later addressed the difficult moment on his podcast “The Pivot,” delivering an emotional response that led to some jabs.

Clark was not the only ESPN personality affected by the company’s layoffs. However, his firing was controversial because he was informed of his termination while on air during “NFL Live.”

The axe fell heavily on Clark as he opened up about his exit on the latest episode of his podcast. He claimed his termination was not performance-based but was linked to his willingness to stand up for his community.

When asked if there were anything he would change about his time at ESPN, Clark became emotional, saying that all he ever wanted was “to be accepted.” He paused several times while trying to regain his composure as tears streamed down his face and his voice cracked.

Clark’s reaction didn’t bode well with many, including Outkick’s Clay Travis.

“I can’t believe this is real. Some people should just stay off social media. It breaks them. Ryan Clark is on his show crying about being fired,” Travis wrote.

“This is pathetic!” former NFL player turned broadcaster Dan Sileo wrote.

“This is utterly embarrassing. Clark needs an intervention. Today,” one podcaster wrote.

Clark also revealed on the podcast that Stephen A. Smith had previously warned him about tensions within ESPN, saying that a particular executive did not like him. Clark said someone inside the company contacted him during the offseason to praise his advocacy for his community, but also cautioned that it had also created powerful enemies among network executives.

Speculation that Clark’s position could be at risk had circulated since the Super Bowl in February, but he admitted he never expected the move to come to pass. That likely contributed to his emotional reaction, though many criticized the way he expressed his feelings.

“Always a victim,” broadcaster Dan Dakich wrote.

“Have some backbone dude it’s rough racket and this proves you can dish it out but not take it. Soft serve,” two-time Emmy winner Mike North wrote.

Clark’s firing came as part of ESPN’s broader round of layoffs tied to its merger with NFL Network. Other well-known personalities, including Karl Ravech, David Lloyd, Cam Newton, Bart Scott, and Andreas Hale, were also among those let go.

ESPN hasn’t directly addressed Clark’s exit, but some other big employees have, including Smith, who later revealed that ESPN executives know he is unhappy about Clark’s firing.

Smith also acknowledged that he wished he had held more influence within the company so he could have prevented the decision. His frustration is understandable, as Clark established himself as one of ESPN’s most recognizable NFL analysts and earned a Sports Emmy Award for Outstanding Personality/Studio Analyst in 2023.

title: Nathaniel Hackett's "definitely a rookie" remark about Jeremiyah Love is getting overblown
description: We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem.
fullText:
We're in the business of finding and sharing and analyzing interesting remarks from anyone in the NFL ecosystem. But certain supposedly controversial comments aren't really as big of a deal as some may interpret them to be.

Case in point: Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett is catching some heat for comments he made on Saturday about rookie running back Jeremiyah Love.

"He's definitely a rookie, and — as we've talked about," Hackett said. "And he'll keep growing every single day. I'm very excited for him. All those guys. Not just him."

The broader context has to be considered, especially since Hackett specifically added "as we've talked about."

Earlier in the session, Hackett addressed the challenges that first-year players face when training camp opens. The question related to the things that are different for rookies.

"Everything you can imagine," Hackett said. "I mean, coming to this league is — I mean, just the speed is so different. You talk about the speed, being in a new building. . . . [I]t's a whole new environment. New people to work with, and definitely new playbooks that are very, very intricate. Due to the fact of all the things that we see and all the different — I mean, just our defense out there. I mean, you get almost everything and more. Which is great, because it helps you for the season, but for a young player to have to be able to adjust and learn just basic system and then apply it to different defenses. It takes some time. So heads are spinning right now, especially after two days, but I think it'll just get better and better. That's the goal."

Hackett wasn't dismissing or minimizing Love. He's a rookie. Like the rest of the rookies. Everything is different. Everything is new. "Heads are spinning," as Hackett said.

Training camp is the time to slow, and eventually to stop, the spinning. They have plenty of time to get Love ready to go. For now, after only two days, he's beginning the adjustment.

That's all it means. Which makes the comment not nearly as alarming as some are making it out to be.

title: Patriots DT Christian Barmore has strong message for rest of the NFL
description: Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore has one goal in mind every time the defense steps on the field.
fullText:
New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore has one goal in mind every time the defense steps onto the field: to dominate.

The star defender spoke with media members after Sunday's practice, where the top defensive unit got the better of the offense. Granted, the Patriots are still hosting non-padded practices, but the competition has remained intense throughout the first couple of training camp sessions.

Justin Herbert, C.J. Stroud and Jarrett Stidham were all on the receiving end of the unit's incredible run. Barmore finished the season with 29 tackles, two sacks and 58 quarterback pressures. title: Report: NFLPA investigating Panthers for possible CBA violation. Here's why
description: The NFL Players Association is investigating the Carolina Panthers for the circumstances surrounding Nic Scourton's recent ACL tear.
fullText:
The NFL Players Association is investigating the Carolina Panthers.

According to Joe Person of The Athletic, the NFLPA plans to examine the circumstances surrounding second-year edge rusher Nic Scourton's injury. Scourton tore his ACL on the first day of Panthers training camp, on Thursday, July 23.

Per Person, the NFLPA will be looking into whether the Panthers were following the rules of an acclimation period to begin training camp that are laid out in the league and union's Collective Bargaining Agreement. The CBA's guidelines state that live contact is prohibited during the first five days of training camp, and that the first day of camp "shall be limited to physical examinations, meetings, and classroom instruction; no on-field activities shall be permitted other than running and conditioning."

NIC SCOURTON: Panthers LB carted off with knee injury at training camp. Latest updates

The NFLPA's investigation will determine whether the Panthers were following protocol and if Scourton's injury was of a non-contact variety. If they review the video of Carolina's practice and determine otherwise, the team could face punishment for violating the CBA.

Scourton, 21, was a second-round pick by the Panthers in the 2025 NFL Draft. As a rookie last year, he appeared in all 17 games, starting eight of them, and recorded five sacks. Heading into 2026, Scourton was set for a potential breakout year playing alongside Carolina's top-flight free agent linebacker signings: Jaelan Phillips and Devin Lloyd. Instead, he likely will miss all of the 2026 season with a torn ACL.

This is a developing story that will be updated.

title: Roster Rankings: Do Dallas Cowboys Boast NFL's Best 'Triplets'?
description: When it comes to offensive firepower, the Cowboys are better than most, but are they at No. 1?
fullText:
FRISCO - When we hear the word "Triplets,'' every Dallas Cowboys follower is able to speak the language.

One word. And we think of Emmitt Smith, Troy Aikman and Michael Irvin.

History has forgotten the origin. ... They weren't "The Triplets'' until after a couple of Super Bowls, and there was no PR power behind it.

In fact, the legendary sportswriter Frank Luksa coined the phrase, rather innocuously at the time.

And for everyone who was involved with or who was a witness to the "Team of the '90's'' Cowboys, there's been a great effort to attempt to assemble a core-group trio to match Dallas'.

A star quarterback, a stud running back, and an elite receiver.

It can be hard to accomplish all of that in the salary cap era; it does seem like the top teams in football often have a top-10-caliber player at two positions before coming up a bit shy of a super-trio ... let alone an Aikman/Emmitt/Irvin triumverate.

So, what about the Cowboys in 2026?

QB Dak Prescott is coming off one of the best years of his career, throwing for 4,552 yards and 30 TDs; Javonte Williams had a career year with 1,201 yards and 11 TDs; and CeeDee Lamb, while having a down year, still produced 1,070 yards and three TDs.

That is a productive trio, no doubt.

Now, if we are ranking all NFL teams' "Triplets,'' where would Dallas land?

CBS Sports has done that exercise, and the publication has the Cowboys' trio of Dak, Javonte and CeeDee at No. 5.

"Prescott led the NFL in completions and had another 30-touchdown year, while his interception rate once again declined,'' CBS Sports writes.

"Williams put together a better-than-expected debut year in Dallas, and Lamb remains one of the best receivers in the NFL. If we'd been allowed to include multiple receivers in these trios, the Cowboys might've ranked even more highly due to the presence of George Pickens."

No. 10 - Philadelphia - Jalen Hurts, RB: Saquon Barkley, WR: DeVonta Smith.

No. 9 - New England - Drake Maye, RB: Rhamondre Stevenson, WR: A.J. Brown.

No. 8 - San Francisco - Brock Purdy, RB: Christian McCaffrey, WR: Mike Evans.

No. 7 - Buffalo - Josh Allen, RB: James Cook, WR: D.J. Moore.

No. 6 - Kansas City - Patrick Mahomes, RB: Kenneth Walker III, WR: Rashee Rice.

No. 5 - Dallas - Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb.

No. 4 - Baltimore - Lamar Jackson, RB: Derrick Henry, WR: Zay Flowers.

No. 3 - Detroit - Jared Goff, RB: Jahmyr Gibbs, WR: Amon-Ra St. Brown.

No. 2 - Los Angeles - Matthew Stafford, RB: Kyren Williams, WR: Puka Nacua.

No. 1 - Cincinnati - Joe Burrow, RB: Chase Brown, WR: Ja'Marr Chase.

We're digging through this list and we have no real argument with it. ... as the Cowboys are obviously among the NFL's elite. (Maybe Dallas' "Triplets'' are superior to Baltimore's?)

This is a subjective barroom debate, of course. Any "anti-Dallas'' thoughts? Well, Lamb had a down year and Williams only has one good season of production. ... but that's pretty nitpicky.

Put it all together and "These Triplets'' mark another reason for Dallas fans to be hopeful about what 2026 can bring, given the offensive firepower coach Brian Schottenheimer has at his disposal.

Oh, and even though the math doesn't add up - there is no such thing as "Four Triplets'' - George Pickens can't be forgotten in the football part of this equation.

In the end? The ranking demonstrates that the Cowboys have all the tools to once again be a dominant force on offense in 2026.

Dak is coming off a Pro Bowl year, Williams has a chip on his shoulder to prove last season wasn't a fluke, and Lamb has Pickens to push him to new heights.

So, do the Cowboys have the fifth-best set of "Triplets" in football? Should they be ranked higher? Or are they the beneficiaries of "America's Team'' hype?

That, friends, is how we start a barroom argument!

title: Former NFL offensive lineman Jorday Devey dies at 38
description: Jordan Devey, who played for five NFL teams over eight years, has died.
fullText:
Jordan Devey, who played for five NFL teams over eight years, has died. He was 38.

Via Jeremy Tombs of Fox 13 in Salt Lake City, Devey died by suicide. His parents told Tombs that they believe Devey suffered from CTE.

Undrafted in 2013 out of Memphis, Devey initially signed with the Ravens but was released. He landed on the Patriots' roster in 2013 and 2014, winning a Super Bowl ring to cap his second year in New England.

Devey spent 2015 with the 49ers, 2016 through 2018 with the Chiefs, 2019 with the Raiders, and 2020 with the Bills. He appeared in 44 regular-season games with 21 starts.

We extend our condolences to Devey's family, friends, teammates and coaches.

title: Mike McDaniel Could Be Under a Microscope This Season
description: Mike McDaniel has another opportunity to prove he’s one of the NFL’s brightest offensive minds. With Justin Herbert under center, success could put him back in the head coaching conversation while failure could reshape his reputation.
fullText:
When the Los Angeles Chargers hired Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator, they weren’t just adding another coach to the staff. They were bringing in one of the NFL’s most respected offensive minds, despite how his tenure as the Miami Dolphins’ head coach ultimately ended.

Now, the spotlight is on McDaniel in a way it hasn’t been in years.

His time in Miami was a tale of two stories. There were moments when his offense looked nearly unstoppable, built around speed, creativity and explosive play design. But as expectations grew, so did the criticism. The Dolphins struggled to consistently beat elite opponents and never made the deep playoff run many expected. Eventually, Miami decided it was time to move in a different direction.

That doesn’t erase McDaniel’s reputation as one of football’s brightest offensive innovators. If anything, it gives him an opportunity to remind everyone why he became a head coach in the first place.

This time, he has something he never had in Miami: Justin Herbert.

Few quarterbacks possess Herbert’s combination of arm talent, intelligence and toughness. While Tua Tagovailoa thrived in McDaniel’s system when healthy, Herbert offers a different dimension. He can attack every area of the field, make throws from impossible angles and create explosive plays even when protection breaks down.

That combination should make Chargers fans excited. It also raises the expectations.

The Chargers didn’t bring McDaniel in simply to maintain what they had. They hired him because they believe he can elevate an offense that has the pieces to become one of the league’s best. Herbert is entering another prime season. Omarion Hampton gives the offense a dynamic young running back, Ladd McConkey continues to develop into one of the NFL’s better young receivers and the offensive line has the talent to be among the league’s better units if it stays healthy.

If the offense takes a significant leap, McDaniel’s reputation will be restored almost overnight. Around the NFL, successful coordinators are always among the first names mentioned when head coaching vacancies open. Pairing an explosive offense with Herbert could quickly put McDaniel back on every owner’s shortlist.

On the other hand, if the Chargers’ offense stagnates or fails to maximize Herbert’s talent, the conversation changes. Fair or not, people will begin to wonder whether McDaniel’s previous success was more dependent on circumstances than his coaching. Questions that surfaced during the end of his Miami tenure will only become louder.

That’s why this season feels so important for him.

Coordinators rarely receive as much attention as head coaches, but McDaniel is an exception. His previous success, his innovative reputation and the opportunity to coach one of the league’s premier quarterbacks make this one of the NFL’s most fascinating storylines.

The Chargers have built a roster capable of competing for a championship. If McDaniel unlocks another level from Herbert and the offense, he’ll likely find himself back in the head coaching conversation sooner rather than later.

If not, this season may force the league to reevaluate just how much of an offensive genius he truly is.

title: Houston Texans Legend DeAndre Hopkins’ Next Career Move Is Completely Unexpected
description: The five-time Pro Bowler may swap his cleats for a clipboard, reuniting with Mike Vrabel in New England to mentor a new generation of NFL talent.
fullText:
After a decorated 13-year NFL career, former Houston Texans wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins could soon be beginning a new chapter on the sidelines instead of the field.

According to reports, Hopkins recently met with the New England Patriots to discuss a potential coaching role on Mike Vrabel's staff. The two are already very familiar with one another, having spent four seasons together in Houston from 2014 through 2017. Vrabel served as the Texans' linebackers coach and later defensive coordinator during that stretch, while Hopkins established himself as one of the league's premier wide receivers.

#Patriots HC Mike Vrabel says WR DeAndre Hopkins is with the team helping out in a potential coaching/personnel role as he figures out his future and what he wants to do next. pic.twitter.com/OY0t9N5gdp

— Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) July 24, 2026

Although the two worked on opposite sides of the ball, they were part of some of the Texans' most successful teams of that era. Hopkins developed into the focal point of Houston's offense, earning multiple Pro Bowl selections and first-team All-Pro honors while consistently producing despite frequent changes at quarterback. Vrabel quickly built a reputation as one of the NFL's brightest young coaches before eventually becoming the Tennessee Titans' head coach.

Their shared history makes the Patriots a logical landing spot if Hopkins decides coaching is the next step in his football journey. Vrabel has always emphasized relationships and accountability throughout his coaching career, and bringing in a respected former player who commanded the locker room during his playing days fits that philosophy.

Hopkins would also have plenty to offer New England's young receiving corps. Few receivers of his generation possessed his combination of elite hands, body control, route-running precision, and ability to win contested catches. Those traits helped him remain productive for well over a decade, and that knowledge could prove valuable for developing younger players trying to establish themselves in the league.

For Texans fans, the news serves as another reminder of Hopkins' lasting impact on the franchise. Drafted in the first round in 2013, he became one of the greatest receivers in team history, recording 632 receptions for 8,602 yards and 54 touchdowns during his seven seasons in Houston. Even years after his departure, Hopkins remains closely associated with some of the franchise's best teams and biggest moments.

Whether this meeting ultimately leads to an official coaching position remains to be seen, but it is an intriguing development for one of the most accomplished players in Texans history. If Hopkins decides his playing days are behind him, reuniting with Vrabel could be the perfect way to begin the next phase of his football career.

title: Where does Vikings' Caleb Banks land in 2026 NFL Draft redo?
description: Caleb Banks fell from No. 18 to No. 29 in a Sports Illustrated 2026 NFL Draft redo, but the Vikings rookie still remained a first-round talent.
fullText:
Caleb Banks has not played a regular-season snap for the Minnesota Vikings, but his draft value is already being revisited.

In a Sports Illustrated 2026 NFL Draft redo published before training camp, Justin Melo had Banks falling to the Kansas City Chiefs at No. 29 overall. The Vikings originally selected the Florida defensive tackle at No. 18, betting on his rare size, power and upside despite an injury history that complicated his pre-draft evaluation.

Melo sent Banks to Kansas City in place of Peter Woods, writing that the Chiefs prioritized defensive tackle in the original draft but could have landed a better prospect in Banks. He described Banks as a “high-risk, high-reward prospect” and noted that playing next to Chris Jones would have been an ideal environment for the rookie to develop.

For Minnesota, the redo reflects the same tension that surrounded Banks throughout the draft process.

His talent was never difficult to identify. At 6-foot-6 and 327 pounds, Banks has the frame and physical tools teams covet in an interior defender. When healthy and consistent, he has the ability to disrupt blocking schemes, collapse pockets and give the Vikings another young building block for Brian Flores’ defense.

The concern has been availability. Banks twice broke his left foot in the past year, an injury that cost him most of the 2025 season at Florida and required surgery after the NFL scouting combine in March. He later sent a letter to NFL teams identifying the injury as a broken fourth metatarsal and projecting that he would resume football activities in June.

That context explains why a redraft can view Banks two ways. The Vikings may have taken on more risk than some teams preferred at No. 18, but SI’s redo still kept him in the first round. That matters.

Minnesota drafted Banks for what he can become, not just what he was able to show during an injury-shortened final college season. Training camp will provide the first real indication of whether that upside is ready to surface quickly.

title: ESPN weighs in on positives, negatives of the Cardinals' young talent
description: ESPN ranks the Arizona Cardinals' under-25 talent towards the top of the NFC West, as they stay in the same NFL-wide ranking as they had last year.
fullText:
ESPN ranked all 32 NFL teams' under-25 talent, and has the Arizona Cardinals at No. 19, the same ranking as last year.

Being in the bottom half of the NFL is nothing for the Cardinals to smile about, especially when they are in the bottom half of the NFL for the second year in a row. Arizona must have needed a higher influx of young talent this offseason if they wanted to improve in these rankings, after the likes of starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. and starting cornerback Garrett Williams turned 25 years old this offseason.

Something for the Cardinals to smile about, however, is where the team stacks up within their division. Other than the Cardinals, every NFC West team won at least one playoff game last season, and both teams in the NFC Championship Game were NFC West teams (Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams). The Seahawks even won the Super Bowl.

The Seahawks are the only NFC West team ahead of the Cardinals on this list, though, coming in at No. 8. The Cardinals are ahead of both the NFC West's San Francisco 49ers (who rank 27th) and the Rams (who rank last). Now, Aaron Schatz — the ESPN writer who wrote the piece that ranked the teams — made it clear that "you don't need to have young talent to be a Super Bowl contender."

"Who needs the long term when you have so much veteran talent in the short term?" Schatz asked when referring to the Rams as the current Super Bowl favorites.

The plus for the Cardinals, though, is some of the first- and second-round picks under the age of 25 who are set to come back from injury this year. 2024 No. 4 overall NFL draft selection and wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is one of them, and Schatz labeled him a "blue chip." "Blue chips" in this context "are the top 60 cornerstone assets around the league from whom teams will likely derive their biggest future value."

Second-round draft pick from 2024 Trey Benson is expected to be back from injury as the season approaches, and the running back has averaged 4.9 yards per carry in his NFL career. Cardinals' first-round defensive lineman Walter Nolen has been working to get back from injury this offseason, and he had five tackles for loss in his six games played in his rookie 2025 season.

Another plus is the under-25 talent in the cornerback room, with 23-year-old cornerbacks Denzel Burke and Will Johnson posting at least 10 PD's each for the Cardinals in 2025.

Lastly, the Cardinals have another "blue chip" in No. 3 overall 2026 NFL Draft selection Jeremiyah Love. The running back is coming off a season in which he was a Heisman Finalist at Notre Dame and a Consensus All-American.

The Cardinals barely crack ESPN's top 20 in terms of under-25 talent league-wide, and haven't improved their ranking from last year. They do rank favorably vs. two of three divisional opponents, however, and rank in the top half of their conference.

title: Ranking the Denver Broncos’ defensive position groups prior to training camp
description: The Denver Broncos have one of the best defenses in the National Football League. How would you rank their position groups?
fullText:
Over the past two seasons, the Denver Broncos have sported one of the best defenses in the National Football League. Under the leadership of Vance Joseph, the team has embarked on a significant turnaround since his first year back leading the defense in 2023. They’ve led the NFL and posted franchise record breaking sack numbers in back-to-back years.

In order to achieve their goal of earning a fourth Lombardi Trophy, the defense is going to have to perform impeccably again this season. Leading up to training camp, here is my ranking of the Broncos’ defensive position groups. Feel free to offer your rankings and reasoning in the comments section.

The Broncos boast the best slate of corners in the NFL. I don’t believe that’s debatable. In fact, I bet every team wishes they had a starting trio of cornerbacks like Denver possesses.

Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian are head and shoulders above the competition. That formidable trio is set to lead the way at the position once again in 2026. After them, Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron are good players who would easily start for most any other franchise.

They do a fantastic job at limiting big plays down the field. Denver’s cornerback prowess was a big reason why they ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage and yards per attempt. They tied for fifth in touchdowns allowed and ranked seventh-best in yards per game.

While there were several pick-sixes by the group in ‘25, Denver’s defense only had 10 interceptions for the entire season. That’s something I’m optimistic will change for their upcoming ‘26 gridiron campaign. In fact, I believe they have ability to be one of the best in the league this season if they live up to their potential.

Denver’s group of edge rushers are definitely a big strength. They are a huge reason why the defense was able to put up eye-popping sack totals in ‘24 and ‘25. However, I have them just a smidge behind the cornerbacks in the overall positional group rankings.

There is no doubt fifth-year pro Nik Bonitto is the top player within the unit. After posting 27.5 sacks the past two seasons, Bonitto has earned two Pro-Bowl nods and is well on his way to an All-Pro honor in the future. His get-off at the line of scrimmage is amongst the league’s best. Moreover, his astounding 20-percent pressure rate is something Defensive Coordinator’s dream of with their edge rushers.

While I’m high the trio of Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman, the potential absence of Jonathon Cooper—at least for a portion of the season due to off the field issues—could become an issue. Cooper has been an underrated performer for the team. While his sack numbers waned down the stretch, his pressure rate of nearly 14-percent is Top 20 at the position.

Can Denver’s group of edge rushers pave the way for them to lead the league in sacks for a third straight season? I think so, but I wonder more if they have what it takes to get more sacks than they did last season. If so, that would be quite the accomplishment.

The departure of John Franklin-Myers to the Tennessee Titans is the main reason I have Denver’s defensive line group ranked third. Even with Franklin-Myers gone, they still have one top-tier performer at the position. Zach Allen is one of the team’s best players and one of the most underrated defensive trench players in the NFL. He’ll lead the way for the group upfront and is poised to have another dominant season.

Outside of Allen, I do like the depth they have. Nose tackle D.J. Jones has been a solid and reliable defender for the team since signing with them several seasons ago. Malcolm Roach was a good addition in last year’s free agent cycle. Fourth-year pro Eyioma Uwazurike could be a breakout candidate for the team this year and will be first in line to help offset the loss of Franklin-Myers.

The big question is how well and how much Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim will play this year. The franchise’s third round picks the past two drafts, both have tantalizing traits and pass rushing skills. But will they be able to flash enough in camp to show they are worthy of significant snaps this year? I can’t wait to find out.

I don’t consider the safety position to be a liability. It’s just that the three aforementioned positions have superior production, impact, and talent levels. Nevertheless, both Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga are quality starters and are certainly an underrated backend duo.

My big question is the depth behind them. In the event either Jones or Hufanga were to miss time, the Broncos would be banking on players with mostly special team’s experience to take over and start. However, potentially sliding Jahdae Barron back there could also be a part of the equation.

Devon Key is an All-Pro player on special teams. Boasting top-tier physical traits, JL Skinner has been a mainstay on special teams the past few years, but very little experience in games defensively. Tycen Anderson, the free agent signing from the Cincinnati Bengals, has virtually the same story as Skinner. Miles Scott was a ballhawk at Illinois, though is still a virtual unknown as a late-round rookie selection.

Your mileage may vary, but the position group on defense that concerns me the most is inside linebacker. It’s a shame the Dre Greenlaw experiment didn’t pan out. I was cautiously optimistic about the signing, but in the end, his inability to stay healthy was the primary culprit in his early exit from the Mile High City.

Given such, Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad will be the Broncos’ starting tandem on the inside. This was one area I thought they may have been aggressive in free agency upgrading. Yet continuity and knowledge of the defensive system meant a lot to the coaching staff and front office.

Outside of Singleton and Strnad, Denver’s group of inside linebackers doesn’t have a lot of NFL experience—especially when it comes to starting. Five players, most all of them UDFAs from the past several years, will be vying for several backup spots on the roster.

Jordan Turner, Levelle Bailey, Karene Reid, Red Murdock, and Taurean York will be in a fierce competition. That just might be the most heated position battle in all of training camp. These players won’t just be looking to prove themselves on special teams, they will be given the opportunity to show they have what it takes to start if called upon.

title: NFL Analyst Identifies the Vikings Player Under the Most Pressure
description: Minnesota Vikings tight end T. J. Hockenson could be in line to have a big year, and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis seems optimistic about where the tight end could head in 2026.The tight end can produce at a high level that much is clear. Just take the 2025 season for example.
fullText:
Minnesota Vikings tight end T. J. Hockenson could be in line to have a big year, and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis seems optimistic about where the tight end could head in 2026.

The tight end can produce at a high level that much is clear. Just take the 2025 season for example. He played in only 15 games, but recorded 51 receptions on 66 targets, for 438 yards and three touchdowns. It was the lowest total of his career, but he still managed to produce at a high level. He missed the final two games of the season with a shoulder injury.

Now, Lewis is predicting this season will be important with a new contract looming.

Critical season forthcoming. Hockenson’s current contract voids after 2026. He is 29 years old. Proving he can produce like he did pre-ACL tear could net another hefty deal.

The 2025 season saw him record 66 receptions for 438 yards and three touchdowns. The tight end was still trying to find that explosiveness he lost following his late-2023 ACL\MCL tear. It showed in some aspects of his play as well. He had a 5.2 average depth of target, which was one of the lower numbers of his career. In addition to not running deeper routes, he also had four drops on 66 targets. This saw him record a 6% drop rate, which was the highest of his career.

In addition, Hockenson was forced to block more. This was a result of inconsistent quarterback play and poor offensive line play. Overall, it was not a good season for a tight end who was one of the most explosive in the NFL at one time.

For his Vikings career, he has recorded 223 receptions for 2,213 yards and eight touchdowns. His best season came in 2023. He had 95 receptions for 960 yards and six touchdowns. He also had a 74.8 catch percentage. To be fair, he recorded the highest catch percentage of his Vikings career at 77.3 in 2025. However, his production was obviously down.

Now, he is looking to bounce back in a major way. The injuries, in combination with an inconsistent offense, have led him to having a reduced role in some ways. This could be his biggest chance to get a strong season under his belt. If he can stay healthy and show that he can perform with the quarterback under center, then he should be able to land himself that new deal. However, the ACL injury certainly looms large, especially for a player who takes pride in receiving and blocking. How he can move this season, two years removed from injury, is going to be important.

When healthy, Hockenson is a valuable piece of the offense. He showed that explosiveness with the Detroit Lions, and he has the opportunity to show it with the Minnesota Vikings as well. At his peak, he can be a game-changer for any offense. Now, he just has to get back to that. Of course, that is easier said than done, but the Vikings’ offense would undoubtedly benefit from him being healthy, as well as taking on more responsibility in the passing game. This will undoubtedly be a storyline heading into training camp.

title: Jon Sumrall is the bluntest talent evaluating coach ever
description: Want a blunt evaluation of your NFL Draft stock? Jon Sumrall seems like the type that would give it to you.
fullText:
First year Florida head coach Jon Sumrall does not sugarcoat it. If you want an accurate assessment of where you stand as a player, how good or bad you are, Sumrall could likely tell you. Want a blunt evaluation of your NFL Draft stock? Sumrall seems like the type that would give it to you.

It's no secret that Florida will be building their offense around talented tailback Jadan Baugh, one of the top running back prospects in in the class of 2027, this season. The Gators are breaking in a new QB1, and according to Sumrall, he won't have to exactly set the college football world on fire with his play, this season.

"None of them need to be Tim Tebow," Sumrall said at SEC Media Days, alluding to the man who won a Heisman Trophy and two national championships in Gainesville.

"They need to be somebody that just manages a game and operates the right way at the line scrimmage and doesn't turn the football over. We've got decent skill players around the quarterback position with Jadan Baugh and the receiver group."

In saying "game manager" and "hey, just don't turn the ball over," Sumrall is basically saying "you don't have to be good, but just don't be awful."

Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo is said to have the slight upper hand in the QB competition right now. However, he faces a stiff training camp position battle against second year Gators QB Tramell Jones Jr.

Sumrall expounded more on the quarterback situation:

"Do we have a Heisman Trophy candidate? No, but they both have enough arm talent. They both are adequate runners. Neither one of them are elite runners. Neither one of them are slugs either. Both have good arms, both have good releases. Both can make all the throws. So there's enough there for us to win with."

Again he makes the QB room sound pretty mid right now.

Sumrall is going viral right now for his faking outrage over a reporter's cellphone going off in the middle of his media session.

While it's meant as a compliment to the league where "it just means more," it also just serves a joke right up on a silver platter. Or at least it does for those who might be cynical about how the SEC may have operated in the pre-NIL era.

title: Jake Paul claims NFL teams have reached out to sign him to address ‘super mediocrity’ among players
description: Jake Paul might be eyeing a major career transition, as he pivots from the boxing ring to the NFL gridiron. Paul is perhaps the most polarizing figure in all of sports today.
fullText:
Jake Paul might be eyeing a major career transition, as he pivots from the boxing ring to the NFL gridiron.

Paul is perhaps the most polarizing figure in all of sports today. And he has managed to translate his notorious reputation into a lucrative career as one of the biggest draws in combat sports today.

But after a crushing defeat to Anthony Joshua in December, could Paul be leaving behind his gloves for a helmet and some shoulder pads?

Speaking to Front Office Sports, Jake Paul revealed that he has had conversations with multiple NFL teams and coaches about possibly transitioning to the NFL.

Paul then took a dig at a large number of NFL players, suggesting that he is a better athlete than them, and that he would pursue an NFL career once he wraps up his boxing career.

“It’s pretty simple. Just like when I started boxing, it’s funny to see the Tweet-and-deleters out there, the non-believers, the non-sayers, shoutout to Drake.

“I think there is a lot of super-mediocrity in the NFL, a lot of not-good athletes, a lot of people dropping passes on a consistent basis.

“I have better hands than them, I’m faster than them, I’m stronger than them, I work harder than them. Really, all it is going to take is just me after boxing, practicing some routes.

“I have a couple of teams and coaches that I have talked to that are interested in bringing me on to the team. It’s really going to be quite easy.”

When asked which team in the NFL he would want to play for, Paul claimed that he wanted to represent his hometown team, the Cleveland Browns.

“I’d love to go to the Cleveland Browns, I’ve been a Browns fan my whole entire life. My mom is a die-hard Browns fan and I think they could use some good receivers over there. Reserve the #17 Browns jersey right now, thank you.”

Paul grew up in Cleveland, so his desire to play for the Browns makes sense, especially considering their lack of success over the last two decades.

It appears Paul is trying to transition from combat sports to football, something Brock Lesnar attempted in 2004 when he left the WWE.

Lesnar managed to make it to the Minnesota Vikings practice squad before being cut, but the University of Minnesota standout had some prior high school football experience to justify the endeavor.

Paul does not have the same football experience, nor the explosive athleticism that Lesnar did, so he might find this transition a lot tougher.

title: LA Rams’ Matthew Stafford Falls to NFL MVP for Best QB in Latest Rankings
description: The Los Angeles Rams spent the offseason feeling like Matthew Stafford is one of the NFL’s otherworldly quarterbacks for at least one more season.A new national ranking offered an endorsement that bolstered that belief.FOX Sports’ Henry McKenna ranked all 32 projected starting quarterbacks heading into training camp and placed Stafford at No. 2.Only Buffalo Bills […] The post LA Rams’ Matthew Stafford Falls to NFL MVP for Best QB in Latest Rankings appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams spent the offseason feeling like Matthew Stafford is one of the NFL’s otherworldly quarterbacks for at least one more season.

A new national ranking offered an endorsement that bolstered that belief.

FOX Sports’ Henry McKenna ranked all 32 projected starting quarterbacks heading into training camp and placed Stafford at No. 2.

Only Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen finished above him.

Stafford landed ahead of Joe Burrow, Jordan Love, Justin Herbert, Drake Maye and Patrick Mahomes.

McKenna described the exercise as an early look toward Week 1, with quarterback readiness, supporting casts and track records among the considerations.

The placement gives the Rams another reason to enter training camp with Super Bowl expectations.

Stafford earned the ranking after producing the best statistical season of his 17-year career.

The 38-year-old led the NFL with 4,707 passing yards and 46 touchdown passes while throwing eight interceptions. He also finished second with a 109.2 passer rating, led the league with 236 passing first downs and helped Los Angeles finish 12-5.

His efficiency became historic during the middle of the season.

Stafford became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw at least four touchdown passes without an interception in three consecutive regular-season games. He later set a league record by throwing 28 consecutive touchdown passes without an interception.

Those numbers earned Stafford the first Associated Press NFL MVP of his career and a first Associated Press NFL MVP. The Rams then signed him to a contract extension in May, removing one potential distraction before his 18th season.

The ranking still stopped one place short of putting Stafford at the top.

Allen passed for 3,668 yards with 25 touchdowns and 10 interceptions last season, although his rushing ability continues to give Buffalo another dimension.

FOX Sports nevertheless placed Stafford above several younger quarterbacks carrying their own championship expectations.

That group includes Mahomes, who fell to No. 7 as he works back from a torn ACL, and Burrow, who ranked third after an injury-shortened season.

For Stafford, No. 2 represents another sign that age has done little to weaken his standing around the league.

The regular-season production only tells part of the story.

Stafford completed 22 of 35 passes for 374 yards and three touchdowns in the NFC Championship Game. The Rams still fell 31-27 to the Seattle Seahawks after defensive and special teams mistakes left the offense chasing the game.

According to the Rams, Stafford became the first quarterback to throw for at least 350 yards and three touchdowns without a turnover and lose a playoff start. Puka Nacua caught nine passes for 165 yards and a touchdown, but Los Angeles could not complete its final comeback.

That ending reinforced how close the Rams are to another Super Bowl appearance.

Los Angeles selected Ty Simpson with the No. 13 pick in the 2026 NFL draft as Stafford’s eventual successor. The Rams have not established a timeline for that transition, and Stafford said during organized team activities that his body felt good as he prepared for another season.

Training camp begins July 27 at Loyola Marymount University. The Rams can manage Stafford’s workload while developing the depth behind him, but there is little uncertainty about which quarterback determines the team’s ceiling.

FOX Sports placed Stafford behind one quarterback in the league.

After an MVP season and a narrow NFC Championship Game loss, the Rams enter camp with expectations to match that ranking.

Stafford has already shown he can play at the required level. The next challenge is turning it into one more Super Bowl run.

title: ‘This Is Huge’ – NFL Podcaster Alleges New Evidence in Matt Miller Fantasy League Scandal

fullText:
ESPN’s NFL Draft analyst Matt Miller has been making headlines recently, but it has had nothing to do with football.

Instead, it’s because he’s being investigated by the Missouri attorney general for allegedly scamming his followers out of money he promised would go toward charity. This comes after a devastating car accident that required multiple surgeries and a life-saving amputation of his arm.

Now, one NFL podcaster provided some new information on Miller’s alleged scam, resurfacing audio of Miller’s brother potentially incriminating himself.

Earlier this month, the Missouri Attorney General’s Office opened an investigation into Miller. This was in response to numerous people coming forward and alleging that the ESPN analyst was scamming his followers using charity fantasy football leagues.

Miller allegedly started many leagues with an entry fee of $100, with half of the pot supposedly going to charity. However, many of the league’s winners never received their winnings, and there was no proof that the other half of the funds had been sent to charity. title: Carson Beck first among top 4 QBs drafted to sign rookie deal

Beck signed his rookie deal, the Arizona Cardinals announced Wednesday. All seven members of the Cardinals’ 2026 draft class, who reported to training camp Wednesday, have now inked their rookie deals.

Beck was drafted in the third round (pick No. 65) in this year’s draft. The 24-year-old rookie is expected to battle with Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew for Arizona’s starting quarterback job.

Beck played 55 college games with Miami (2025) and Georgia (2020-24). He passed for 11,725 yards and 88 touchdowns while compiling a 37-6 record as a starter.

According to Over The Cap, Beck’s four-year contract is worth $7.4 million.

Rookie contracts are slotted and predetermined. But the top four quarterbacks selected in the 2026 draft, Fernando Mendoza, Ty Simpson, Carson Beck and Drew Allar, were all unsigned as of Wednesday morning because of unresolved terms in their contracts.

Quarterbacks typically to have more leverage to negotiate certain details in their rookie contracts. Signing bonus cash flow, guaranteed money details and offset language are negotiable terms in rookie contracts.

Beck, Simpson and Allar are represented by agents part of the Creative Artists Agency (CAA) while Mendoza is represented by an agent in Excel Sports Management.

Now that Beck has signed his rookie deal, expect it to have a domino effect on the rest of the QB rookie class.

title: Rams fall to dead last in new ESPN ranking
description: The Rams roster is one of the oldest in the NFL but also doesn't have too much talent under the age of 25.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams may have one of the best rosters on paper, but it's mainly constructed of veterans rather than long-term developmental players. As such, the Rams' roster ranks 26th-oldest heading into the 2026 season.

This isn't a bad thing, especially for a team with immediate Super Bowl aspirations spearheaded by a 38-year-old quarterback, but it means they checked in at No. 32 in ESPN's latest ranking of NFL teams' under-25 talent.

ESPN built the rankings using starts and snaps logged by players under 25, age-adjusted quality of play with extra weight for Pro Bowl and All-Pro selections, contract value and length, positional importance, draft capital added in the first three rounds of the 2026 draft, projected 2026 depth charts, and any injuries or suspensions likely to affect availability.

Unsurprisingly, the Rams don't have many of those types of players on their roster at the moment.

Perhaps you have heard that the Rams are not as fond of first-round draft picks as other teams? Certainly, trades they have made for veterans contribute to the fact that while Los Angeles has a ton of talent, very little of it is under 25 years old.

The Rams only had two players currently under 25 who started games last season: safety Kamren Kinchens, who will be 24 at the end of September, and tight end Terrance Ferguson, who is also 23. Another one of the tight ends, second-round rookie Max Klare, just turned 23 on July 8. First-round quarterback Simpson will turn 24 in December. The Rams hope Simpson doesn't get on the field for a couple of seasons because they have someone much older they would rather see under center: reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, who is 38 years old.

First-round quarterback Ty Simpson is the lone player ESPN tabs as a blue chip for the Rams' under-25 core, and even he isn't expected to see the field anytime soon behind Stafford. Compounding the shortage, Los Angeles just graduated several of its best young pieces out of eligibility: cornerback Trent McDuffie, offensive tackle Warren McClendon Jr. and wide receiver Puka Nacua all turned 25 and no longer count toward the rankings.

That combination — an aging roster built through trades and free agency, a limited draft footprint and a wave of players aging out right as they hit their prime — leaves the Rams with the league's thinnest projected young talent pool heading into 2026, according to ESPN.

But again, that won't matter if they bring home a Lombardi Trophy.

fullText:
Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis has broken his silence on the demand for NFL teams to use grass fields on the back of this summer’s World Cup.

The Allegiant Stadium was not one of the host venues for the United States at the World Cup, but it is one of the NFL stadiums that uses a natural grass playing surface.

There is an argument to be made that a natural surface is easier for Vegas to maintain given it is an indoor venue, which does not expose the grass to the elements.

However, Davis is one of the owners who believes playing on a grass field is largely beneficial for his players’ health and wellbeing.

This is not a view that is shared across the league, with numerous NFL players now protesting their thoughts after seeing grass pitches laid down for the World Cup soccer teams.

As the Dallas Cowboys have already ripped up their grass field at AT&T Stadium, Davis has issued a message on the importance of his players playing on a natural surface.

In recent days, Seattle Seahawks fans have urged their new owners to lay down a grass surface at Lumen Field.

It is proving the hottest topic of discussion across the league, as the players make their voices heard over social media.

“There was no way I was going to build the stadium or anything else to play on artificial turf,” said the 71-year-old.

“I just always felt that the safety issue, number one, and I grew up around football and the grass and mud and the smell of those uniforms after the game.”

The Raiders’ stadium cost just shy of $2 billion to build and Davis did not cost cut by going with an artificial playing surface for his players.

Pat McAfee has backed the NFL players’ protest for grass fields, with Davis also backing the notion it should be an investment from the owners towards their players’ safety.

Owners across the league are happy to pay out huge wages to their star players, but there is a clear hesitation from some of them to splash out on installing and maintaining a grass field.

Witnessing the same stadiums across the nation suddenly install grass for the World Cup will have come as a slap in the face for NFL players across the league.

This is why the movement is picking up steam ahead of the 2026 season getting underway.

title: Patrick Mahomes’ changing appearance through the years has NFL fans saying the same thing

Patrick Mahomes has collected three Super Bowl championships, three Super Bowl MVP awards and two NFL MVP honors during his remarkable run with the Kansas City Chiefs. Yet after seeing how the quarterback’s appearance has changed over the years, NFL fans were left wondering whether Mahomes has aged at all.

Mahomes has endured plenty of wear and tear while developing into one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history. His latest challenge is a torn ACL suffered in December, an injury that has made his recovery one of the biggest storylines surrounding Kansas City entering the 2026 season.

Despite everything Mahomes has experienced since becoming the Chiefs’ starting quarterback, a collection of photos posted Tuesday had fans making the same observation.

He really does not look much different.

The NFL shared a series of photos on Instagram showing Mahomes from 2019 through the 2026 offseason. Although there were a few noticeable changes, including different headbands, fewer wristbands, shorter hair and a thicker goatee, Mahomes’ overall appearance remained strikingly similar.

That immediately caught the attention of fans.

“He looks the exact same. Is he AI?” one fan wrote, according to Athlon Sports.

“Looks exactly the same! Love you Patrick!” another fan commented.

“He hasn’t aged, he just gets more handsome,” one reaction read.

Another fan asked a simple question: “Does he age??? He looks the same.”

“Never will age!!!!” another person added.

The side-by-side comparison was especially interesting because of everything that has happened during the period covered by the photos.

Mahomes was only beginning to establish himself as the face of the NFL in 2019. He had already won his first league MVP award, but his championship run in Kansas City was just getting started. Since then, Mahomes has led the Chiefs to three Super Bowl victories and established himself as the defining quarterback of his generation. Kansas City selected him with the No. 10 overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft, and he has spent his entire career with the franchise.

His resume has changed dramatically. His appearance apparently has not.

While fans had fun with the photos, Mahomes is currently dealing with a far more serious issue. The Chiefs quarterback continues to recover from the torn ACL he suffered in December. Reports have suggested that he could return as early as Week 1, although Kansas City will have to carefully monitor his progress leading into the season.

The injury came during a disappointing year for the Chiefs, who missed the playoffs for the first time since Mahomes became their full-time starting quarterback. Kansas City responded by making several notable offseason moves.

The Chiefs re-signed longtime Mahomes target Travis Kelce and acquired reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III to strengthen the offense. They also signed Justin Fields, giving the team an experienced option at quarterback while Mahomes works his way back. Fields could provide important insurance if Mahomes is not cleared for the season opener. If Mahomes is ready, Fields could still give Kansas City additional flexibility as a backup and situational weapon.

The Chiefs are counting on those additions to help them return to the postseason, but their championship hopes will ultimately depend on Mahomes’ health. The quarterback in the 2026 photo might look almost identical to the player pictured seven years earlier. Getting back to playing like that younger version of himself after a major knee injury will be the much more important challenge.

title: The men behind Trump's $3.47 gas: An NFL coach, a GOP fundraiser and two New Jersey brothers
description: President Donald Trump and his White House have enthusiastically promoted the Freedom Fuel Network, a chain of star-spangled convenience stores selling gas at $3.47 per gallon in honor of the 47th pre...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump and his White House have enthusiastically promoted the Freedom Fuel Network, a chain of star-spangled convenience stores selling gas at $3.47 per gallon in honor of the 47th president.

Untangling exactly who is behind the Philadelphia-area venture has proven difficult. Records indicate the chain, which was launched last month, is run by a disparate collection of businessmen that includes an NFL kicking coach, a GOP fundraiser and a New Jersey entrepreneur who this year was ordered, along with his brother, to pay civil damages for unlawfully taking more than 200,000 gallons of fuel.

How the stations got Trump's attention remains a mystery, and the four businessmen declined to — or could not be reached for — comment.

What is clear: Trump loved the idea of cheaper gas. The president celebrated the network's gas prices just before the busy July 4th travel period as consumers were grappling with higher oil prices sparked by the war with Iran.

"I am pleased to announce that a VERY smart Retailer, located throughout the Northeast, is stepping up," Trump wrote about the company on his Truth Social platform on July 1. "America has never been stronger than it is now, and Gas Prices will soon be back to the Record Low Prices Americans enjoyed at the pump before our very successful 'excursion' in Iran."

The White House followed up with a post on X a few days later that heralded the opening of the first Freedom Fuel station and produced a video showing patrons waving wads of cash and thanking Trump for reducing the prices outside a store festooned with American flags and a golden eagle logo.

That station, located in Dresher, Pennsylvania, is owned by a subsidiary of Blue Owl Capital, an investment firm, records show. Trump has owned up to $25 million worth of Blue Owl stock, though his most recent financial disclosure says he has sold almost all of that stake.

The White House denied Trump had any personal connection to the venture, but declined to say how the project was developed. It acknowledged having discussions with individuals who set up the network of gas stations.

"The Administration is not involved in the company, nor has the Administration given the company any funding. There is no other entity or person subsidizing the lower gasoline costs," the White House wrote in a statement.

Blue Owl owns about a third of the Freedom Fuel properties, though the company said it leases the stores to independent contractors and "is not involved in the tenant's operations or business decisions."

Fourteen stations in the 25-location network are controlled by companies linked to Shamikh and Syed Kazmi, two brothers who have been dogged by a string of civil misconduct accusations, including fraud, records show.

Shamikh Kazmi is leasing eight of those stations from Blue Owl, according to state records and people familiar with the businesses who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the matter. The Associated Press was able to link the brothers to six other Freedom Network locations through records that show they listed those stations' addresses as headquarters for other ventures or supplied those locations with fuel.

A White House official, who insisted on anonymity to discuss the project, said that no one at the White House who was in conversations with Freedom Fuel Network had specifically spoken or worked with Syed Kazmi, a claim that indicates discussions occurred with the other brother, Shamikh.

The Kazmis have marketed themselves as "top tier" petroleum distributors and gas station operators, with over 75 years of experience and a deep well of corporate affiliations, according to an archived version of the website for one of their companies.

Public records offer a more nuanced portrait, showing the Kazmis have been repeatedly sued by companies they had dealings with.

Legal filings detail a series of judgments against the Kazmis, who failed to comply with a court order and have been accused of obscuring their finances and dodging service processors as a growing list of former suppliers and franchisors sought payment.

In February, a federal judge in New Jersey ordered the Kazmis to pay over $600,000 to a fuel supplier that accused the brothers of stealing gas. The supplier alleged in court filings that it cut the brothers off after they refused to sign a new contract. But the Kazmis exploited a security lapse and gained access to the supplier's fuel depot. Over a ten-day period in August 2021, tanker trucks absconded with more than 230,000 gallons of fuel, according to the supplier's court filings. A judge ruled in the supplier's favor, finding the brothers unlawfully took the gas.

The fuel supplier says it has yet to receive payment.

Syed Kazmi was hit with a $380,000 judgment two years ago in a suit brought by 7-Eleven, the convenience chain, which accused him of "dishonest, unethical, immoral" conduct while operating a franchise in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, that was flagged for unsanitary conditions that included trash issues and a rodent infestation. The company also said "tens of thousands of dollars" of cigarettes ordered from 7-Eleven on credit had gone missing.

A federal judge held a company operated by Shamikh Kazmi in contempt in 2022 in a trademark case brought by BP America.

Though BP had severed ties with Kazmi's Diwan Petrol two years prior to the legal action, the corporation's signage had not been removed from the gas station despite a court order to do so. The judge authorized U.S. Marshals to accompany BP workers to remove it.

A man who answered a call to a number listed for the Kazmi brothers said he was not the right person to talk to and instead directed inquiries to the Freedom Fuel Network's website. But that website has no contact information, phone number or mailing address. A request for comment submitted through an online contact form was not answered.

Records from Delaware, a state known for offering incorporators a large degree of opacity, show the Freedom Fuel Network was registered on June 23. The document forming the company was signed by Randy Brown and Yoni Gontownik.

Politico and the website The Newsground reported that Brown is a senior special teams coach with the Baltimore Ravens. He has also served as the elected mayor of Evesham Township, a New Jersey suburb of Philadelphia, where a Freedom Fuel Network station is located.

Brown, a Republican, considered a run for Congress in 2021, telling a local newspaper he was a conservative and a "proud Trump supporter."

Gontownik is a former investment director at Mercuria, a Swiss-owned commodities trading firm. He and his wife live in northern New Jersey and have been active with the pro-Israel political action committee NORPAC, including hosting fundraisers for Republican members of Congress.

Gontownik and Brown did not respond to requests for comment.

Jeff Lenard, a spokesman for the National Association of Convenience Stores, said Freedom Fuel's rock bottom promotional price meant the chain was likely selling the gas at a loss.

"It's not unusual for retailers to have prices that are different than a market when they're looking to make a splash," said Lenard, whose association's members account for most U.S. retail fuel sales, adding that such a splash typically lasts "a matter of hours or a matter of days."

Social media posts and gas-price checking websites show that the per-gallon rate advertised at Freedom Fuel locations began creeping up this week.

A Freedom Fuel station in Bensalem, Pennsylvania, for example, on Thursday was selling regular gasoline for $3.82 a gallon. That was 27 cents cheaper than at a Sunoco station across the street.

The Freedom Fuel Network posted a note of thanks to its website this week, crediting Trump's "strong endorsement" for the "explosive growth" of their business.

"Despite the misinformation and baseless speculation circulating," the statement reads, "let us set the record straight: Freedom Fuel Network is proudly lowering its prices to benefit our community."

title: Ex-Eagles Star Gets Necessary Trade Push From NFL Analyst
description: All NFL offseason long, Josh Sweat’s name has been tossed in trade rumors. The former Philadelphia Eagles defensive end has been described as frustrated with the Arizona Cardinals. When OTAs were starting up across the league, many NFL rumors hinted that Sweat could see a change. The Eagles were often linked as trade candidates for […] The post Ex-Eagles Star Gets Necessary Trade Push From NFL Analyst appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
All NFL offseason long, Josh Sweat’s name has been tossed in trade rumors. The former Philadelphia Eagles defensive end has been described as frustrated with the Arizona Cardinals.

When OTAs were starting up across the league, many NFL rumors hinted that Sweat could see a change. The Eagles were often linked as trade candidates for their former draft pick.

But with training camp quickly approaching, the Sweat rumor mill has gone silent. Bleacher Report’s NFL writer Moe Moton is pushing the Cardinals to kick it back up, by listing a Sweat trade as something that needs to get done before training camp.

GLENDALE, ARIZONA – NOVEMBER 23: Josh Sweat #10 of the Arizona Cardinals looks on from the line in the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at State Farm Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images)

“Josh Sweat needs a change of scenery,” Moton wrote.

“He’s played most of his career with the Philadelphia Eagles, a perennial playoff contender. This offseason, the Arizona Cardinals fired lead skipper Jonathan Gannon, who coached the veteran edge-rusher during their time together in Philadelphia.”

Sweat is reportedly unhappy in Arizona, as Moton noted. He is a win-now player, coming from a competitive NFC team. Sweat was recruited by his ex-Eagles coordinator. Now that Gannon’s out of the picture, the situation seems to be difficult for Sweat to overcome.

GLENDALE, ARIZONA – OCTOBER 05: Josh Sweat #10 of the Arizona Cardinals during the NFL game at State Farm Stadium on October 05, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. The Titans defeated the Cardinals 22-21. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images)

In the same rundown of moves that need to happen, Moton suggested the Eagles should pick up the veteran defensive end, Von Miller. It would be easier, as Miller is a free agent and would require just a one-year commitment.

Sweat, on the other hand, is going into year two of a four-year, $76.4 million contract. He’s owed a lot and would need to be acquired via trade. Of course, the Cardinals aren’t going to accept pennies for the 12-sack pass rusher.

PHILADELPHIA, PA – DECEMBER 22: Josh Sweat #94 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates his sack on Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on December 22, 2019 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Philadelphia Eagles defeated the Dallas Cowboys 17-9. (Photo by Corey Perrine/Getty Images)

Making the call is worth it, to at least figure out a price. If it’s within reason, the Eagles shouldn’t hesitate to pounce.

In 17 games with the Cardinals last season, Sweat racked up 30 total tackles, with 13 going for a loss. His 12.0 sacks marked a career high.

The last time the Eagles had Sweat in action, he picked up 41 tackles and 8.0 sacks. During the Super Bowl run, Sweat had 10 tackles, three for a loss, and 2.5 sacks.
